name: Turnaround and quality monitoring
summary: Measuring processing turnaround against per-mode targets, reporting SLA performance to Track3D teams, and showing how much of a capture was processed and which frames were dropped for quality.

roles.note: SLA monitoring is for Track3D operations (TechOps, MLOps) and project managers; coverage and frame quality are also shown to customers in the PRDs. No permission strings exist for these views.

actions.note: Assumes coverage sits on the project's progress pages; not confirmed

nfr.statement: Historical PRD turnaround targets: 360 video and laser processed within 24 hours, 360 images and phone images within 1 hour, with 90% of media processed within those times.
nfr.open_question: Are these still the commitments, and do production deadline settings (VD_SLA_FOR_*, TWOD_SLA_FOR_360V) match them (DEC-056)?

requirements.title: Each capture mode has a processing turnaround target
requirements.statement: 360 video walks and laser data are processed within 24 hours of upload, and 360 images and phone images within 1 hour. Large files must not break these targets. The deadline recorded on each capture is CAPT-REQ-008.

open_checks: The code reads deadline hours from environment settings (CAPT-REQ-008); their production values weren't read

requirements.title: When the turnaround clock stops
requirements.statement: The PRD measures visual turnaround from upload to the visual snapshot becoming active, and progress turnaround from upload to the progress snapshot becoming active. The code stops the visual clock at different events: for 360 and phone images when a reality is first made active (or at a time the caller supplies), and for 360 video, drone and laser when the job's outcome becomes active, partialProcessed or error. A failed job therefore stops the clock and can count as met.

dispute.summary: The PRD stops the clock at snapshot activation; the code stops it at reality activation for image modes and at any final job outcome, including error, for 360 video, drone and laser. It also accepts a caller-supplied completion time.

requirements.title: TechOps can monitor SLA performance across captures
requirements.statement: Track3D teams can list captures uploaded in a date range, see each capture's SLA as passed, missed or pending, and filter by project, company, capture type, date, camera type and pipeline type. SLA metrics show the average, minimum and maximum. A status change after the first calculation triggers recalculation.

requirements.title: Show capture coverage against processed coverage
requirements.statement: For a floor plan, users see how much area was captured and how much was successfully processed, side by side. Captured but unprocessed areas are highlighted, uncaptured areas are left uncoloured, and areas with low capture or processing coverage raise an alert.

requirements.title: Show every extracted frame, marking low-quality ones
requirements.statement: The walkthrough for a 360 video shows all frames extracted from the video, including ones left out of processing for quality. Low-quality frames carry a distinct marker, missing positions are interpolated from neighbouring frames, and users can switch between all frames and processed frames only.
